newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Surging milling wheat futures in focus in Budapest.
newsitem.headline: Surging milling wheat futures in focus in Budapest.

text.p: Milling wheat futures dominated trade on the grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Friday as two major players sought to close short positions, traders said.
"It was mainly LaSalle and Order," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
Milling wheat futures generally rose by the daily 400-forint limit and accounted for the overwhelming majority of today's turnover.
Total grains turnover rose to 441.2 million forints from Thursday's 234.6 million, with 817 milling wheat contracts out of the total 966.
May milling wheat closed at 25,340 forints per tonne, up 340, while new (1997) crop maturities rose mostly by 400 forints to finish between 21,800 forints for July and 25,000 forints for March 1998.
October was the only milling wheat position that bucked the trend, easing 50 forints to 23,100.
Maize turnover remained light with most of the fairly balanced trade concentrated on the two nearest maturities, May and July.
Prices remained flat at 18,500 forints for May and 17,500 for July. Tradeless March 1998 rose to 20,500 forints.
Monostori said old crop prices were likely to drift lower as current prices could persuade producers to appear on the selling side.
Feed wheat and feed barley rose mostly in line with milling wheat but only saw minimal turnover of five contracts each, for October feed barley and July feed wheat.
